Prevention: Use seed or dry sets free from pathogen
Avoid over application of cattle manure
Avoid excess nitrogen application as too much nitrogen will soften cells making it easier for the pathogen to infect the crop
Practice 4 year crop rotation to reduce the build- up of the pathogen in the soil
Eradicate volunteer onions near the field
Destroy plant debris after harvesting by burningDestroy plant debris after harvesting by burning
For seed crop, use rain shelters or spray water to remove dew
Monitoring: Make regular field visits and observe field for infestation
Look especially at older leaves as they are more commonly affected than younger tissues
Initial symptoms are white coloured spots on leaves.
Over time, these lesions become brown and finally purple
In seed crops flowers become brown
